newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Jordan to expand bromine venture.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Jordan to expand bromine venture.

text.p: Israel's Dead Sea Bromine Group and Jordan's Arab Potash Company (APC) have agreed to increase the size of a joint venture for bromine production , an Israel Chemicals spokesman said.
Dead Sea Bromine is a subsidiary of Israel Chemicals.

The initial agreement between the two companies called for the proposed joint plant to produce 25,000 tons of bromine compounds and the two companies have now agreed in principle to increase this to 35,000 tons.

The spokesman said the investment in the proposed joint venture would increase from $50 million to $80 million. The initial memorandum of understanding for the setting up of the venture was signed last year at the Amman economic summit.

The decision to increase the size of the venture emerged from negotiations between the two companies in recent weeks and comes amid a serious deterioration of relations between the two countries in light of the lack of progress in the peace process.
Israeli sources said a final agreement on the proposed plan could come as early as next week.
The plant will be located on the Jordanian side of the Dead Sea, rich in bromine. Both companies have production facilities on opposite sides of the Dead Sea.
Dead Sea Bromine is one of the world's largest producers of bromine. Dead Sea Works, another subsidiary of Israel Chemicals, produces potash.
APC currently produces only potash but for some time has been interested in expanding its actvities into bromine.

Chlorine, used in the production of bromine, will come from Dead Sea Magnesium, a joint venture between Dead Sea Works and Volkswagen AG, which is due to begin production of magnesium at the end of the year.
